subject.title: Session paths resolve through symlinks, causing false-positive doctor orphans

question: Should maintainers import/review the linked fork PR as the fix path, or wait to queue a fresh same-repository repair if that external candidate stalls?
rationale: The bug is narrow and source-reproducible, but the currently open closing reference is outside the target repository and cannot be treated as a normal OpenClaw PR landing path by this cleanup review.

options.title: Import or review the fork PR
options.body: Use the open fork PR as the implementation source if maintainers can convert it into a reviewable target-repository branch with proof.

options.title: Queue a fresh repair later
options.body: Keep this issue open and queue a new focused repair only after maintainers decide the fork PR will not be reviewed or imported.

options.title: Manual tracker only
options.body: Leave this issue open without automation until a maintainer manually owns the symlinked session-path fix.

recommendation.title: Import or review the fork PR
recommendation.body: Use the open fork PR as the implementation source if maintainers can convert it into a reviewable target-repository branch with proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant resolver behavior is tied most directly to their session path hardening work.
